name: IL-15
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Mary Miller running with large financial edge
Democratic challenger raised only $113k with no outside support
model.rationale: The R+20 district, Miller's incumbency and roughly twelve-to-one fundraising advantage, and markets pricing her at 96% all point the same direction, with no polls or expert ratings suggesting any vulnerability. The forecast sits near the fundamentals-based margin with a slight adjustment for the incumbent's resources.
model.watch: A major national Democratic wave environment or unexpected scandal could narrow the margin, though flipping the seat remains highly unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Republican incumbent Mary Miller seeks reelection in a heavily Republican southern Illinois district with a partisan lean of about R+20. She enters the general election with a large financial advantage, having raised roughly $1.3 million and holding over $800,000 on hand, while Democrat Jennifer Todd has raised about $113,000 with minimal outside spending on either side. No public general-election polls are available, and no expert raters list the race as competitive.

Prediction markets give Miller about a 96% chance of winning. The fundamentals point to a comfortable Republican margin, with the district lean and incumbency outweighing a modestly favorable national environment for Democrats. The race is rated Safe Republican, with the main question being the size of the victory rather than the outcome.
